1.
This is first appeal preferred by some of the lega

l representatives of original plaintiff no. 1 (since deceased) against Judgment and Decree dated 28.01.2026 passed in CS no.9/2017 (hereinafter referred to as 'the impugned Judgment/Decree').
2.
There were eight original plaintiffs before the trial court and plaintiff no. 2 to plaintiff no. 8 have not challenged the impugned judgment and decree.
Again, plaintiff no. 1 appears to have expired during trial and eight of his legal heirs were brought on record.
Three of them (three daughters of original plaintiff no. 1) have also not challenged the impugned judgment and decree.
3. Only the five sons of original plaintiff no. 1 who were P-1(i) to P-1(v) before the trial court have challenged the impugned judgment and decree.
4. For the sake of convenience, parties shall be referred to by the nomenclature used in the Ld. Trial Court.

Brief Facts:
5. One Natthi Singh (original plaintiff no. 1) along with other plaintiffs claimed that they are in possession of 3 bighas of land (out of total land measuring 64 bigha and 5 biswa) falling in Khasra No. 89/3/2 situated in Village Ghonda Gujran Khadar, Shahdara, Delhi.

It was their case that they are the owners of the said property by way of RCA DJ 25/26 Natthi Singh (deceased) Through LRs vs. Delhi Development Authority & ors. 2 of 11 revenue records/khatauni and their possession is being threatened by DDA/D-1.

Thus, they prayed for a decree of permanent injunction seeking to restrain the defendants from carrying illegal and unauthorized construction; also restraining them from dispossessing the plaintiffs illegally and forcefully from the said 3 bighas of land (falling in khasra no.89/3/2), Village Ghonda Gujran Khadar, Shahdara, Delhi (hereinafter referred to as 'Suit Property').
6.

The suit was resisted primarily by DDA/D-1 contending that the entire Khasra bearing no. 89/3/2 (measuring 64 bigha 5 biswa) was acquired by DDA and out of it possession of 61 bigha 5 biswa (which includes the suit property) is with DDA.
The possession of the said land stated to have been given to Horticulture Department of DDA for maintaining green area.

7. DDA contended that the 3 bigha of area (which stood acquired from Khasra bearing no. 89/3/2 but whose possession is not taken) falls in Old Usmanpur abadi area which is away from the suit property/land.

In other words, as per DDA, the possession of the acquired area to the extent of 61 bigha 5 biswa (which includes the suit property) has been taken by DDA and the possession of the remaining acquired area measuring 3 bighas is still not taken; but, this area is distinct and separate from the area being claimed/disputed by plaintiffs.
As per DDA, plaintiffs are nothing but encroachers on the land acquired and possessed by DDA.

8. Before proceeding further, it may be noted that as per the plaint set up by the plaintiffs, they themselves claim that the suit property falls RCA DJ 25/26 Natthi Singh (deceased) Through LRs vs.
Delhi Development Authority & ors. 3 of 11 in Khasra no. 89/3/2, Village Ghonda Gujran Khadar,
Natthi Singh (Deceased) Through Its Lrs vs Delhi Development Authority on 25 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118883447/
2 Illaqa Shahdara, Delhi; and as per plaintiffs, an area of 61 bigha 5 biswa vested in gram sabha under the provisions of Section 81 Delhi Reforms Act, 1954 vide order dated 25.09.1979.
I shall come back to this aspect of the matter in a little while.

9. It is also pertinent to note that plaintiffs themselves plead in the plaint that an award no. 8/92-93 has also been passed qua acquisition of the land falling in the above Khasra i.e. 89/3/2, Village Ghonda Gujran Khadar, Shahdara, Delhi.
But, as per the plaintiffs, this award only pertains to 61 bigha & 5 biswa of area of land.
I shall also come back to this aspect of the matter in a little while.

10. The said suit came to be dismissed by way of the impugned judgment/decree inter alia holding that (a) plaintiffs have failed to prove ownership over the suit property; (b) show their possession over the suit property; (c) D-1/DDA, as per plaintiffs' own witnesses has possession of the suit property; (d) plaintiffs are mere encroacher on the suit land already acquired by DDA.
11. I propose to dispose of the present appeal, in limine and therefore, no notice of this appeal was given to the other side.

12. Before coming to the grounds taken in the present appeal, it may be recalled that three LRs of P-1 [who were P-1(vi) to P-1(viii)]; and P-2 to P-8 have not challenged the impugned judgment and decree despite expiry of statutory time for appeal and thus, the decree has attained finality qua the said plaintiffs.
RCA DJ 25/26 Natthi Singh (deceased) Through LRs vs. Delhi Development Authority & ors. 4 of 11 13.

sentences.text: The remaining LRs of P-1, through counsel, argued that the Ld. Trial Court did not appreciate the evidence on record in the correct perspective and failed to note that a khasra khatauni/revenue record can be treated as admissible evidence of possession.

It was the contention of the counsel that based on the said revenue record Ex.PW1/4, P-1 and the other plaintiffs could prove the possession of the suit property and thus, without DDA proving acquisition proceedings qua the disputed land,
the plaintiffs were entitled to the decree in their favour.

It was argued that DDA did not prove the fact that any compensation was actually disbursed to the recorded owners in revenue record Ex.PW1/4 and therefore, the Ld. Trial Court could not return a finding that plaintiffs do not have possession of the suit land.
14. In my humble opinion, neither of the contentions raised by the LRs of P-1 (who are before this court) has any legal basis.

15. Before the trial court, plaintiffs themselves had pleaded a case that the suit property falls in Khasra no. 89/3/2, Village Ghonda Gujran Khadar, Illaqa Shahdara, Delhi; and as per plaintiffs, an area of 61 bigha 5 biswa vested in gram sabha under the provisions of Section 81 Delhi Reforms Act,
1954 vide order dated 25.09.1979.
Plaintiffs themselves relied upon the said order dated 25.09.1979 as Mark A.

A bare perusal of the said order shows that the said order does not pertain to an area of 61 bighas 5 biswas; but in fact it covers an area of 64 bigha and 5 biswa falling in Khasra no. 89/3/2 of Village Ghonda Gujran Khadar, Shahdara, Delhi.

Thus, plaintiffs have pleaded false facts before Natthi Singh (Deceased) Through Its Lrs vs Delhi Development Authority on 25 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118883447/
3

entities.text: Natthi Singh (Deceased) Through Its Lrs vs Delhi Development Authority
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
the Ld. Trial Court by claiming that the RCA DJ 25/26 Natthi Singh (deceased) Through LRs vs.
Delhi Development Authority & ors. 5 of 11 said order pertains to only 61 bigha 5 biswa, when in fact it pertained to 64 bigha 5 biswa of land.
16.
By virtue of the said order, the land measuring 64 bigha and 5 biswa falling in Khasra no. 89/3/2 of Village Ghonda Gujran Khadar, Shahdara, Delhi vested in gram sabha on 25.09.1979 itself.

Thus,
even if it is taken that by virtue of revenue record Ex.PW1/4, plaintiffs or their predecessor in interest were the recorded owners of the land measuring 64 bigha 5 biswa falling in Khasra no.
89/3/2, Village Ghonda Gujran Khadar, by virtue of the above order (Mark A, which has been pleaded and relied upon by plaintiffs themselves), the said land entirely vested in gram sabha on 25.09.1979 and thereafter, plaintiffs or their predecessors or any person claiming through or under them would have no right, title or interest in the said land (till the said land stood vested in gram sabha).
17. It is neither pleaded nor proved on record that the said order was ever set aside.
Thus, on this ground itself, the suit was liable to fail.

18. It is also pertinent to note that plaintiffs themselves plead in the plaint that an award no.
8/92-93 has also been passed qua acquisition of the land falling in the above Khasra i.e. 89/3/2,
Village Ghonda Gujran Khadar, Shahdara, Delhi.
But, as per the plaintiffs, this award only pertains to 61 bigha & 5 biswa of area of land.

19. Now, during the evidence of plaintiffs, they produced one Dinesh Kumar (who was SPA of D-6 and D-7 and was D-8 himself) as RCA DJ 25/26 Natthi Singh (deceased) Through LRs vs. Delhi Development Authority & ors. 6 of 11 PW-2.
This witness, during his cross-examination, was shown the copy of award bearing no. 8/92-93 dated 09.06.1992 and he admitted that the said award pertains to Village Ghonda Gujran Khadar.

The said award was eventually exhibited as Ex.PW2/D1.
20.

A bare perusal of the said award shows that Khasra no. 89/3/2, Village Gujran Khadar was acquired by the concerned Land Acquisition Collector and compensation for the same was calculated by the said award which was payable to the recorded owners.
In the said award, against Khasra No. 89/3/2, the area of acquisition is mentioned as 64 bigha 5 biswa.

Thus, as per the admitted documents of the plaintiffs, the entire Khasra no. 89/3/2, Village Ghonda Gujran Khadar measuring 64 bigha and 5 biswa stood acquired by the concerned LAC and the compensation payable in lieu thereof was calculated.
21. Thus, the contention of the plaintiffs that only 61 bigha & 5 biswa of area (out of 64 bigha & 5 biswa) was acquired by LAC concerned is a false and incorrect fact pleaded by the plaintiffs.
As per the said award, the entire 64 bigha & 5 biswa stood acquired.
22. Plaintiffs had also sought a decree of permanent injunction from the Ld. Trial Court.
The same is an equitable relief.
It is settled law that a person who seeks equity, must do equity and should approach the court with clean hands.

Evidently, plaintiffs had set up false claim qua the suit property by claiming that only 61 bigha 5 biswa of area vested with gram sabha and only that area Natthi Singh (Deceased) Through Its Lrs vs Delhi Development Authority on 25 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118883447/
4 was acquired.

In fact, as per their own documents/admissions, the entire area of 64 bigha & 5 RCA DJ 25/26 Natthi Singh (deceased) Through LRs vs. Delhi Development Authority & ors. 7 of 11 biswa vested in gram sabha and for the said entire area, acquisition took place.

sentences.text: 23. Once the same is shown from the record, plaintiffs do not have any right, title or interest which they can derive from the khasra khatauni Ex.PW1/4 to maintain a simplicitor suit for injunction.
24. It can be argued that even if the plaintiffs do not have any documentary title, still, if they have possessory title, they could maintain a suit for permanent injunction.
But, for showing possessory title, it was essential for the plaintiffs to prove settled possession of the suit land.
25. A perusal of the record would show that plaintiffs simply want to assert their possessory title on the ground that they are rearing some cattle on the suit property.

It has come in the cross-examination of PW-1 that there is no pucca construction in the disputed 3 bighas of land (see cross-examination of PW-1/Natthi Singh dated 17.08.2018); and in the cross-examination of PW-2/Dinesh Kumar that the disputed land is a vacant land without any construction and is used for purpose of cattle grazing (see cross-examination of PW-2 dated 28.05.2025).
Thus, as per the plaintiffs' own case, the disputed land is a vacant piece of plot.
26. It is settled law that in cases of vacant land, de facto possession follows de jure possession.
In other words, only if plaintiffs were able to establish that they had legal title to the suit land, the physical possession of the said land could be treated to be available with the plaintiffs.
But, as already noted, they have no documents.
In fact, the RCA DJ 25/26 Natthi Singh (deceased) Through LRs vs. Delhi Development Authority & ors. 8 of 11 property, as per their own admission, has been acquired.

entities.text: RCA DJ 25/26 Natthi Singh (deceased) Through LRs vs. Delhi Development Authority
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Even otherwise, the property being claimed by the plaintiffs is shown to be a vacant piece of land and for possession to be treated to be that of the plaintiffs, it was necessary for them to prove de jure possession.
They have failed to do so.

27. Merely because plaintiffs have managed to bring some cattle on a vacant area of land shall not mean that they are holding settled physical possession of the land so as to give them possessory title thereto.
28. In fact, as per the cross-examination of PW-2, the suit land is shown in photographs Ex.PW2/2 (colly.) running into 8 pages and the boundary wall seen in the said photographs is of DDA.

29. The relevant portion of said cross-examination reads as under:
"The witness is now shown another set of photographs and is asked the following questions:
Ques: Whether the land shown in the said photograph is the suit land?
Ans: Yes.
Accordingly, the same is Ex.PW2/D2 (colly running into 8 pages).
It is correct that the boundary shown in the photographs Ex.PW2/D2 (first page) is of DDA.......

Natthi Singh (Deceased) Through Its Lrs vs Delhi Development Authority on 25 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118883447/
5

It is correct that there is a boundary wall of DDA on the suit land."
(emphasis supplied)
30.

A bare perusal of the aforesaid cross-examination would show that a boundary wall of DDA/D-1 exists on the disputed land which essentially means that not only the property has been acquired by the concerned LAC, the possession thereof has also been given and is still with DDA/D-1.
31.
Thus, once it is shown that plaintiffs have neither title nor possession of the suit property, the outcome of the suit was sealed.
RCA DJ 25/26 Natthi Singh (deceased) Through LRs vs. Delhi Development Authority & ors. 9 of 11

The Ld. Trial Court had rightly returned the findings that (a) plaintiffs have failed to prove ownership over the suit property; (b) show their possession over the suit property; (c) D-1/DDA, as per plaintiffs' own witnesses has possession of the suit property; (d) plaintiffs are mere encroacher on the suit land already acquired by DDA.

32. Thus, if the plaintiffs wanted to establish any right over the property, it was necessary for them to sue for a declaration of title; challenge the acquisition proceedings; and then sue for consequential relief of possession with injunction.
Nothing of the sort was done and in fact, since the plaintiffs failed to take any steps in the manner described above, the suit was also hit by Section 41(h) of Specific Relief Act, 1963.

The more efficacious remedy for the plaintiffs was to clear their title over the property by seeking a declaration of title (which would also involve challenging the acquisition proceedings before the appropriate forum) and then seek possession.
It appears that plaintiffs have in fact tried to somehow confuse the entire factual scenario by claiming false facts before the court.

It appears that despite being aware of the fact that the suit land measuring 3 bighas falling in Khasra no. 89/3/2, Village Ghonda Gujran Khadar has been acquired way back in 1992 and possession of the same has been taken by LAC about 2 decades back, plaintiffs want to stake claim to a different area by confusing the court that the said area is the same area which falls within the ambit of said acquisition.

It appears that about 3 bigha of area falling in Khasra no. 89/3/2 is yet to be taken possession of and plaintiffs want to take benefit of the RCA DJ 25/26 Natthi Singh (deceased) Through LRs vs. Delhi Development Authority & ors. 10 of 11 same by claiming that this area (whose possession is yet to be taken) is the same area for which they are staking claim.
This is when the area for which the stake is being made already stands in possession of DDA.
33. Be that as it may, for the reasons noted by the Ld. Trial Court and for the reasons supplied in this judgment, the suit of the plaintiff could only meet one fate i.e. dismissal.
It has been rightly dismissed and there is no infirmity in the impugned judgment which calls for any interference by this court.
34. Accordingly, the appeal fails.
It is dismissed.
Let a decree-sheet be prepared accordingly.
35. Let copy of the judgment passed in appeal along with decree-sheet be sent to Ld. Trial Court.
